_comment: How the repository scan agent evolved: the self-improvement loop run behind results/synthetic.md, on all the pairs
it ran on: the public synthetic benchmark and two benchmarks we can't publish, as aggregate counts only. Per version
of the agent: pairs right of the 36 training pairs the loop measured it on, and of the 47 held-out validation pairs;
fixed twins flagged on each. A pair is right when the agent reports the planted lines in the vulnerable repository
and nothing at the same lines of its fixed twin. Each version was built on the one before it. The version presented
is the one with the most validation pairs right; its test result is on 46 test pairs nothing in the loop had seen.
Per version, what the optimizer changed: our own one-line summary, the size of the change, and a few of the lines
it added (from its prompt, its tools' descriptions, its pipeline). The optimizer's own notes are not used: they cite
repositories of the benchmarks we can't publish.

versions.label: Start
versions.summary: The starting point, written by hand and deliberately weak: a short prompt, and tools to read files and run Python.
Looks at the whole repository, not file by file: a first pass marks risky lines everywhere, and a last check withdraws findings whose safeguard is in place.
highlights: Work like a diff reviewer. Real defects in this kind of code are single statements where one
specific control is missing; the rest of the repository is normal, ordinary code.

versions.summary: Compares like with like: a new tool shows how the same kind of statement is written across the repository, so the one that differs stands out.
highlights: Every repository already contains the *reference form* of the operation you are looking at
Compare how one family of statements is written across the whole repository.

versions.summary: Reports as soon as it is sure instead of running out of steps, and a new tool lists the odd one out among similar statements.
highlights: Report first, analyse later. You have a hard step limit and a finding you never filed helps nobody
'Odd one out' census of the repository's sink sites.

versions.summary: Adds a step that makes no model calls: it checks where the project applies its own safeguards, and where it doesn't.
Learns more defect patterns, such as a path check that '..' gets around, and tells real safeguards from look-alikes.
highlights: - a containment test written in text form - `str(root / value).startswith(str(root))` - in code
that never resolves the path: `..` segments keep the prefix, so the test passes for a path that
steps outside the root. The test line is the finding.

versions.summary: Adds a second step without model calls, for patterns such as a secret passed on a command line or a path that escapes its folder.
Fewer false alarms: a step without model calls withdraws findings on lines already written the safe way.
highlights: `escape_*` helper, `secure_filename`, or a temporary-file helper is correct code - do NOT report it

note: The counts include two benchmarks we can't publish.
